When I say that this is what a follow up game done right looks like, I seriously mean it. This took all of the good aspects of Risky's Revenge and kept them, and the flaws were improved upon so much, that this is just a super good experience throughout.

There isn't a single thing I really have to complain about when it comes to this game. I found the graphics are really nice and charming. Personally, I really like the idea of having a pixel style game with more detailed sprites, I feel like thats something the Shantae franchise does that no other franchise does super often, and it's a really unique approach to a game aesthetic. I honestly found the idea of Shantae and Risky Boots teaming up really interesting, and it had me sucked in the entire time. A hero and a villain both teaming up for a game, and the fact that they both have polar opposite, yet really charming and lovable personalities only made the story so much better. I think they both go really well together, they're a sweet duo that you gotta love.

What surprised me the most was just how much they improved the map system and the overall layout of the world compared to Risky's Revenge. I found that the layout of the world and the map was super difficult to follow in Risky's Revenge, to the point where I got stuck multiple times and needed a guide to even know where to go next (this was the only flaw in that game, and it was great in every other aspect), whereas the map and world layout in this game is so much cleaner and easier to follow, that it just made the game so much better. I didn't really need any pointers to know where to go, the map was super straightforward and clean, and it just led to an overall amazing experience.

Overall, Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is a significant step up from Risky's Revenge, as it keeps what made the previous game great, and improved on what kept it flawed. The characters are loveable, the story is amazing, the gameplay is clean, and the map is much easier to follow. I can't recommend this game enough. If you got stuck on Risky's Revenge, and found the layout made it difficult to progress, please try this game. I can't stress enough just how much of an improvement Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is!

[h1]All Achievements Review[/h1]
[b]My Playtime:[/b] 11h (100% achievements, finished the game)

[b]Grindy Achievement(s):[/b] No.
[b]Optional Achievement(s):[/b] Yes (Multiple speedrun endings and 100% completion).

[h3]Pros:[/h3]

[b]Responsive controls:[/b] Moving Shantae feels very precise, which is great for the platforming sections.

[b]Fun power ups:[/b] The pirate gear (Pistol, Hat, Cannon) provides a fun twist on traditional Metroidvania abilities.

[b]Upgradeable skills:[/b] Progression feels steady as you buy hair-whip speed and damage upgrades.

[b]Nice pixel graphics:[/b] The character art and environments are vibrant and look great on a modern screen. Even though max in-game resolution is 1080p.

[h3]Cons:[/h3]

[b]Far too easy:[/b] Unlike some of the harder titles in the genre, I managed to finish this without dying once.

[b]Bad level design:[/b] There is a frustrating amount of backtracking and constant revisiting of the same locations.

[b]Bosses are a joke:[/b] The boss fights are super easy and require very little strategy to overcome.

It can be hard to figure out where to go next sometimes due to vague NPC hints.

[hr]

[h3]Length and Difficulty[/h3]
The game is relatively short. If you know what you are doing, you can 100% it in under 10 hours. I’m guessing the "effective" playtime for most players is around 8-12 hours across two playthroughs (one for 100% and one for the <2 hour speedrun achievement).

Difficulty is non-existent if you've played any other platformers or Metroidvanias. Most bosses can be tanked simply by using buffs, spamming your hair whip and bosses will be dead within seconds. The platforming only gets slightly tricky in the very final area. If you're looking for a challenge, you won't find it here.

[h2]Verdict[/h2]
[b]5/10
A decent platformer for beginners, but lacks depth and challenge for veterans of the genre.[/b]

Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is widely regarded as one of the strongest entries in the long-running Shantae series, developed and published by WayForward. Blending tight platforming, vibrant pixel art, and a cleverly structured Metroidvania progression system, it refines the franchise’s formula into something both accessible and mechanically satisfying. Originally released on handheld systems before arriving on Steam, the game stands as a confident reimagining of its heroine’s abilities and a high point for 2D action-platformers in the modern era.

The story begins with Shantae stripped of her genie powers following the events of the previous game. Rather than restoring her magic, Pirate’s Curse pivots in a bold direction by having her team up with her longtime rival, the pirate captain Risky Boots. This partnership forms the emotional and mechanical backbone of the adventure. While the narrative itself remains lighthearted and often comedic, it benefits from sharp writing, expressive character portraits, and a sense of momentum that keeps players engaged between action segments. The banter between Shantae and Risky Boots adds personality and charm without overwhelming the pacing.

Mechanically, the loss of Shantae’s traditional transformations becomes one of the game’s greatest strengths. Instead of animal morph abilities, she gains access to pirate-themed gear that doubles as combat tools and traversal upgrades. The flintlock pistol, pirate hat glide, scimitar, and cannon are not only useful in battle but also essential for exploration. This design creates a more cohesive progression system compared to earlier entries. Each newly acquired tool unlocks shortcuts, hidden rooms, and alternate pathways across the game’s interconnected islands. The result is a steady sense of growth and empowerment tied directly to exploration.

The world is divided into multiple islands, each with distinct themes, enemies, and environmental challenges. Level design is layered and encourages thorough investigation. Secret passages, hidden collectibles, and optional side quests reward players who take the time to search every corner. While backtracking is required, it rarely feels tedious because new abilities frequently transform previously visited areas into fresh exploration opportunities. The pacing strikes a careful balance between guided progression and player-driven discovery.

Combat is straightforward but polished. Shantae’s primary hair-whip attack remains quick and reliable, while pirate gear adds variety to encounters. Boss fights are memorable and well-designed, often requiring pattern recognition and creative use of newly acquired equipment. Difficulty leans toward moderate, offering enough challenge to keep experienced platformer fans engaged without becoming punishing. Checkpoints are forgiving, allowing experimentation without excessive frustration.

Visually, Pirate’s Curse showcases some of WayForward’s strongest pixel art work. Character animations are fluid and expressive, backgrounds are richly colored, and environmental themes feel distinct without sacrificing cohesion. The art style manages to evoke retro nostalgia while maintaining modern clarity and detail. Complementing the visuals is a standout soundtrack filled with energetic and atmospheric tracks that reinforce each island’s personality. Music plays a significant role in establishing tone, whether during high-intensity boss battles or quieter exploration moments.

Replayability is enhanced through collectibles and unlockable modes. Completionists can hunt for hidden Heart Squids and other secrets that expand health or unlock bonus content. After finishing the game, Pirate Mode becomes available, allowing players to replay the adventure with all abilities unlocked from the start. This significantly changes traversal pacing and encourages speedrunning or optimized routing.

Overall, Shantae and the Pirate’s Curse represents a refined and confident evolution of the series. By replacing magical transformations with pirate gear, it strengthens both combat and exploration mechanics. Combined with charming writing, polished presentation, and thoughtfully crafted level design, it delivers a tightly constructed Metroidvania experience that remains engaging from start to finish. Whether approached as an introduction to the series or revisited by longtime fans, it stands as one of WayForward’s most accomplished platformers and a standout title within the genre.

Rating: 9/10

Лучшая игра серии — №1 в моём личном рейтинге

Если честно, именно Pirate’s Curse — это та игра, с которой для меня началась настоящая любовь к серии Shantae. Я пытался пройти первую и вторую части, но они были запутанными и достаточно сложными. А вот когда я впервые запустил Проклятие Пирата, всё изменилось. Это была игра, которая сразу показала:
«Вот она. Та самая идеальная Shantae.»

И до сих пор, спустя годы, я считаю её лучшией частью серии. Самой сильной. Самой эмоциональной. Самой атмосферной.

⚔ Геймплей — лучшее, что есть в Shantae

После Risky’s Revenge геймплей полностью преобразили.
Shantae потеряла свои магические способности, но взамен получает пиратское снаряжение Risky Boots, которое она осваивает через лабиринты. И это настолько круто, что я буквально кайфовал каждый раз, когда получал новый инструмент.

Пиратские умения дают чувство прогресса, энергию, драйв, открывают новые маршруты и в итоге формируют одну из лучших метроидваний, что я играл.
Игра ощущается идеально собранной, гибкой, динамичной. Ничего лишнего — всё ровно то, что нужно.

🎧 Музыка — Джейк Коффман в своём абсолютном пике

Я не преувеличу: саундтрек Pirate’s Curse — лучший в серии.
Это музыка, от которой у меня мурашки по коже даже сейчас, спустя 3–4 года после первого прохождения.

Стоит только включить любую тему — и всё, меня накрывает ностальгия.
Это та самая игра, где музыка становится эмоцией, рассказывает историю сама по себе.

Особенно финальная музыка в замке мерцающих земель…
Это напряжение, это ощущение надвигающейся катастрофы — просто невероятно.
Когда я проходил финальную полосу препятствий, я и бомбил, и одновременно получал удовольствие.
Мурашки, адреналин, атмосфера — это было что-то особенное.

🌀 Сюжет и атмосфера

Overall a pretty good game. As someone new to the franchise, this felt like a pretty good introduction. There were a few moments of confusion or frustration, but overall the game isn't too difficult. It frankly feels refreshing after burning out on the mastery Silksong constantly demands.

Gameplay wise, the controls and upgrades are solid though not especially unique. I suspect they generate a fair amount of nostalgia for people with more familiarity with previous games. The game also has a number of gimmick sections which switch up gameplay in a generally good way, though they're sometimes a bit annoying.

I was pleasantly surprised by this game's characterization. I've been wary of touching this series because it looks like horny-bait garbage, but it's pretty tasteful in how it manages the fan service. It doesn't feel overbearing, or like a crutch to distract from poor writing (things I'm very familiar with as a former anime fan). The characters and jokes were genuinely endearing, even for a newcomer like me who didn't fully grasp all of the background. Though I do think the game could improve here too; having some optional content to mention Shantae's history with the other characters would've been appreciated. Maybe also throw in some interactions between the main companion character and other NPCs, so I could get a better sense of her reputation (which I only really realized at the very end).

Definitely going to dig into the rest of this series.

I finished the story in this game without having played the first games, the original 2002 Shantae and the more recent Shantae: Risky's Revenge.  Honestly I kind of wish I had played the first one... but it isn't available on Steam and it's a pretty old game at this point.  If you are brand new to Shantae, I would recommend taking a look at the Risky's Revenge game and playing that first.  All the stories kind of interconnect, they use the same characters, and it also really showcases the series' progression from where it started, other than the original 2002.

Now this game is wonderful.  It's a straight up platforming game, and it's on the easier side.  This is meant to be casual.  It's still got some bite to it, though, if you don't watch yourself.  The story is cute and fun, the graphics look great, and the performance is solid.  Just make sure that whatever platform you play this on, you LOCK IT TO 60hz.  If you don't, you'll get odd game speed issues.  Even on PC, I had to use Nvidia control panel to lock the game at 60hz otherwise it ran at like double speed.  On Steam deck, I had to drop the max frame rate down to 60hz from the default 90hz.

All that aside, this game stands out in the series because of the pirate weapons, which are all pretty fun.  They definitely add a new dimension to the gameplay vice the first game.

I'm still playing through the following game right now, Half Genie Hero, which I can tell you is already a very good follow up to this game and adds quite a large amount of new depth and challenge.  That is where the series really starts to modernize.  But this game is an absolute gem to play through, and I recommend it to anyone looking for a light hearted platformer.

Pirate's Curse is a very solid game I would highly recommend, outside of a few small issues that can be pretty irritating. It took me around 8 hours to complete a first playthrough with all items collected. I probably would have saved around an hour or so if I wasn't stubbornly going for the no HP upgrades achievement (which I gave up on 75% of the way through the game).

Pros:
- Looks and sounds great
- Controls feel tight and responsive
- Every area feels visually distinct and all have their own unique gimmicks
- Zelda style dungeons are the highlight, and they do a great job showing off how your new items work
- Pirate tools have use in both combat and exploration. Some can even be used together for some fun results
- The story is surprisingly fun
- Hidden items are placed well
- Plenty of achievements for completionists

Neutral:
- Retro style save system. Die, and you lose all progress since your last savve
- Not particularly difficult for metroidvania veterans
- No difficulty settings
- You can spam items from the inventory to trivialize any hard fight
- There are a couple of gimmicky segments that go on for a long time. The stealth section in particular can be frustrating.

Cons:
- No fast travel. Almost every island requires you to backtrack to a previous island. This becomes problematic on the later islands where you will need at least five minutes just to walk back to where you were.
- Enemy density gets crazy in the later areas. Even with maxed upgrades, it takes awhile to tear through them.
- No map markers.
- You can only view the map for the area you are currently in
